literal: Double-minded women and, liquor and, gambling and, prosperity to-forsake those-who-experience association.
translation: Double-minded women, liquor, and gambling are the companions of those forsaken by prosperity.
modern: உள்ளத்தில் ஒன்றும் வெளியில் ஒன்றுமாக இருக்கும் விலைமகளிர், கள், சூதாட்டம் ஆகிய மூன்றும் செல்வத்தால் கைவிடப்பட்டவர்களின் தொடர்புகள் ஆகும்.
explanation: The couplet groups together three destructive vices: prostitutes, alcohol, and gambling. The phrase 'double-minded women' refers to those who show false affection for money while their true intentions lie elsewhere. The poet states that these three things are the natural companions of people who have been abandoned by prosperity. Indulging in these vices is presented as the defining characteristic of those whose wealth and well-being are completely ruined.
